title: Renaming a field/concept or dropping one on a live app with data
body: Never rename by deleting the old field and adding a new one with a different name -- that reads to the platform as an unrelated drop+add and either refuses (if the table has data) or destroys the old column's data. Instead: (1) Rename -- add `renamedFrom` to the field object (`{"name":"fullName","renamedFrom":"name",...}`) for a field rename, or to the concept object itself (`{"name":"Customer","renamedFrom":"Client",...}`) for a table rename. This applies in place on the next boot -- zero data loss, no acknowledgment needed. (2) New required field on a populated table -- declare a literal `default` (e.g. `"default": "pending"`) so it backfills automatically; a `defaultExpression`-only field or a required bond field is refused (bonds have no automatic backfill -- make it optional instead, or accept the destructive path). (3) Dropping a field/concept is genuinely destructive and needs authorization: run `Build-NpdevApp.ps1 -Upgrade -PlanOnly` first to see the itemized plan and the acknowledgment token, then re-run with `-AcknowledgeDestructive <token>` (or submit `{toFingerprint, ackToken}` to `POST /api/admin/schema-migration/acknowledge` on the CURRENTLY RUNNING app, SUPERUSER-gated, before deploying the new jar). A rename and an unrelated acknowledged drop on the SAME table both apply correctly in the same boot -- the rename never waits on or gets blocked by the drop. (4) AUTHORING POSTURE FOR A NEW APP -- use `schemaLifecycle: {"strategy": "KeepExistingIfCompatible", "allowDestructiveRecreate": false, "destructiveRecreateConfirmation": "", "scope": "NpdevOwnedTablesOnly"}`. All four fields are required by the schema, but `destructiveRecreateConfirmation` only means anything under `DropAndRecreateOnStructureChange`, so leave it empty rather than copying in the `I_UNDERSTAND_TABLE_DATA_WILL_BE_DELETED` string. Copyable worked examples: `AppGen\apps\simple-user-registry-h2local` and `AppGen\apps\npdev_split_model_sample_app`. IMPORTANT -- most definitions shipped in this repo still carry the OLD blanket posture (`DropAndRecreateOnStructureChange` + `allowDestructiveRecreate: true`); that is backward compatibility, NOT a recommendation, so do not infer the intended posture by copying an arbitrary existing app. (5) What the blanket posture actually authorizes, if you meet one: surgical column drops and type narrowings without a token -- and nothing else. Anything that destroys a whole table's worth of data requires the itemized token regardless of the flag: dropping a concept (LNCH-1 hardening X4.4), and any diff that cannot be executed item by item, which would otherwise drop and recreate EVERY table in the app (LNCH-1 closeout C1). Both refuse the boot and print the token that would authorize them. Authorized destructive changes execute SURGICALLY -- only the itemized tables/columns are touched. (6) Dev/CI loops must NOT rely on "just recreate everything on boot": delete the database file/volume between runs, or use a `freshdb`-style definition such as `simple-user-registry-h2local-freshdb`. `strategy: RecreateOnAppStart` is NOT an escape hatch -- despite the name it has no distinct runtime behaviour and recreates nothing. See docs/SCHEMA_EVOLUTION.md for the full worked example.
